info.label: Atlantic
info.desc: Led Zeppelin II is the second studio album by English rock band Led Zeppelin, released 22 October 1969 on Atlantic Records. Recording sessions for the album took place at several locations in the United Kingdom and North America from January to August 1969. Production was entirely credited to lead guitarist and songwriter Jimmy Page, while it also served as Led Zeppelin's first album to utilise the recording techniques of engineer Eddie Kramer. The album furthered the lyrical themes established on their debut album, Led Zeppelin (1969). This progress helped create a work that became more widely acclaimed and influential than .

podcast.body: Released in 1969, this album received strong negative reviews from some critics, with Rolling Stone magazine reportedly "hated the entire album." Despite this, it contained songs like "Whole Lotta Love" that were pushing both musical and sexual boundaries. "Rolling Stone hated the entire album."

Released only a few months after their debut, this album was described as even more profound than its predecessor. It is considered the definitive record marking the transition from the old era of rock to the new. This second album launched with a radically new approach where the guitar was no longer just a refined accompaniment but the central element, with the bass forming an intrinsic, intertwined relationship with it, establishing these two string instruments as dominant. "Y posiblemente el disco segundo del lecepelling, el lecepelling 2 es el disco que marca la transición del viejo rock al nuevo rock."

podcast.body: This album was noted for containing songs that co-opted old blues material, particularly "Bring It On Home" and "The Lemon Song," which were ruled highly derivative of earlier works by Willie Dixon and Howlin' Wolf. "Led Zeppelin was caught doing something similar, co-opting old blues songs as their own, especially with their second album."
